Istanbul-Turkey.name: Istanbul
Istanbul-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1477 Mehmed II tahrir survey (~16,324 hane incl. Galata, Inalcik), 16th-18th c. provisioning and guild registers (Mantran 1962), 1844 count, and 1885/1914 Ottoman censuses (Karpat 1985; Shaw 1978).

Cairo-Egypt.name: Cairo
Cairo-Egypt.evidence_basis: Mamluk peak and Black Death drop, Ottoman intra-mural surveys (Raymond 1984), 1800 Description de l'Egypte (263,000), 1846/48 census (Alleaume & Fargues: 256,000), and 1882/1897/1907/1917 Egyptian Censuses.

Alexandria-Egypt.name: Alexandria
Alexandria-Egypt.evidence_basis: Nadir of ~12,000 in 1800 Description de l'Egypte, explosive growth after 1820 Mahmudiyya Canal and cotton boom (Reimer 1997; 1846 census: 104,128; 1882-1917 Egyptian Censuses).

Izmir-Turkey.name: Izmir
Izmir-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1528 and 1575 Aydin tahrirs showing modest port before 17th-c. Aegean trade boom (Goffman 1990; Frangakis-Syrett 1992), Cuinet (1894: ~200,000), and 1914 Ottoman registers.

Damascus-Syria.name: Damascus
Damascus-Syria.evidence_basis: 1401 Timurid sack dip, 1520/1569 Damascus tahrirs (Bakhit 1982; Raymond 1984), Hajj caravan expansion, Cuinet (1896: 150,000), and 1914 Syria Vilayet census.

Baghdad-Iraq.name: Baghdad
Baghdad-Iraq.evidence_basis: 1401 Timurid sack, 1534/1638 Ottoman conquests, devastating 1831 plague and Tigris flood (~60% loss, Nieuwenhuis 1982; Raymond 1984), Cuinet (1894: 145,000), and 1914 salname.

Algiers-Algeria.name: Algiers
Algiers-Algeria.evidence_basis: Ottoman regency capital (1516-1830) peaking during 17th-c. corsair boom (Raymond 1984; Shuval 1998), ~30,000 at 1830 French conquest, and French Recensements (1856, 1886, 1911).

Tunis-Tunisia.name: Tunis
Tunis-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Hafsid and Ottoman Beylik capital; intra-mural and suburb expansion analyzed by Raymond (1984: ~100,000 in 1700-1800) and French Protectorate 1911 Census (164,608).

Aleppo-Syria.name: Aleppo
Aleppo-Syria.evidence_basis: 1520-1584 Aleppo tahrirs and 1683 avariz survey (Raymond 1984; Marcus 1989), 1822 earthquake contraction, Cuinet (1894: 127,150), and 1914 Ottoman census.

Beirut-Lebanon.name: Beirut
Beirut-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Small coastal town in 1520-1830 Ottoman registers transformed by silk export, steamship port, 1860 Mount Lebanon refugees, and 1888 vilayet capital status (Fawaz 1983; Cuinet 1896).

Oran-Algeria.name: Oran
Oran-Algeria.evidence_basis: Spanish presidio (1509-1792) devastated by 1790 earthquake, Ottoman Western Beylik seat (1792-1831), and booming French port in 1856/1886/1911 Recensements.

Adana-Turkey.name: Adana
Adana-Turkey.evidence_basis: Ramazanid capital; 1523 and 1572 Adana tahrirs (Kurt 1992), 19th-c. Cukurova cotton and 1886 railway boom, Cuinet (1894: 30,000), and 1914 census (Toksoz 2010).

Port Said-Egypt.name: Port Said
Port Said-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded April 1859 at the northern entrance of the Suez Canal; 1869 Suez Canal Company count and exact 1882/1897/1907/1917 Egyptian Censuses.

Edirne-Turkey.name: Edirne
Edirne-Turkey.evidence_basis: Ottoman capital (1365-1453) and late 17th-c. court seat; 1530 tahrir (Barkan 1957: 22,335), 1881-93 and 1914 Ottoman censuses (Karpat 1985).

Bursa-Turkey.name: Bursa
Bursa-Turkey.evidence_basis: First Ottoman capital (1326) and silk hub; 1530 and 1573 Hudavendigar tahrir defters (Barkan & Mericli 1988; Gerber 1988), Cuinet (1894: 76,303), and 1914 census.

Jerusalem-Palestine.name: Jerusalem
Jerusalem-Palestine.evidence_basis: 1525, 1553, and 1596 Ottoman tahrirs (Cohen & Lewis 1978), 19th-c. consular/traveler counts and extra-mural expansion (Ben-Arieh 1975; Scholch 1993), and 1914 Ottoman census.

Mecca-Saudi Arabia.name: Mecca
Mecca-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Ottoman Hejaz suzerainty (1517); resident population estimates by Burckhardt (1814-15), Snouck Hurgronje (1885), Hejaz Vilayet salnames, and steamship Hajj growth (Faroqhi 1994; Ochsenwald 1984).

Tanta-Egypt.name: Tanta
Tanta-Egypt.evidence_basis: Sayyid al-Badawi shrine and Delta railway/cotton hub; 1800 Description de l'Egypte, 1846 census, and exact 1882/1897/1907/1917 Egyptian Censuses.

Mosul-Iraq.name: Mosul
Mosul-Iraq.evidence_basis: 1540/1575 Mosul tahrirs, 18th-c. Jalili-era prosperity (Khoury 1997), 1828-31 famine/plague dip, Cuinet (1894: 61,000), and 1914 Mosul Vilayet salname.

Constantine-Algeria.name: Constantine
Constantine-Algeria.evidence_basis: Ottoman Eastern Beylik capital (1528-1837); Raymond (1984) intra-mural estimate (~25-30k in 1830) and French Algerian Recensements (1856, 1886: 44,960; 1911: 65,173).

Sfax-Tunisia.name: Sfax
Sfax-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Olive-oil, sponge, and Gafsa phosphate export port (1899 railway); Beylical tax records and French Protectorate 1886/1911 enumerations.

Homs-Syria.name: Homs
Homs-Syria.evidence_basis: 1520/1571 Tripoli tahrirs, 19th-c. Orontes silk-cotton weaving and railway boom (1902), Cuinet (1896), and 1914 Syria Vilayet census.

Kayseri-Turkey.name: Kayseri
Kayseri-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1500, 1520, and 1583 Kayseri tahrirs (Jennings 1976: urban surge to ~33k by 1583), commercial guild records, Cuinet (1894: 54,000), and 1914 Ankara salname.

Basra-Iraq.name: Basra
Basra-Iraq.evidence_basis: Shatt al-Arab date and Gulf entrepot; 1773 plague and 1776 Persian siege dip (Fattah 1997), steamship boom at Ashar/Basra complex (Lorimer 1908: ~52,000), and 1914 Basra Vilayet records.

Gözüküçüklü-Turkey.name: Gözüküçüklü
other_names: كوزی كوجكلو و سنده یلانی و پیره لی

Urfa-Turkey.name: Urfa
Urfa-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1518 and 1566 Ruha tahrirs (Turkoglu), caravan/textile prosperity, Cuinet (1894: 55,000), and 1914-18 Aleppo Vilayet / wartime contraction.

Hama-Syria.name: Hama
Hama-Syria.evidence_basis: 1520/1571 Hama tahrirs (Reilly 2002), agrarian grain/textile expansion under Azm and Kilani notables, Cuinet (1896: 44,000), and 1914 census.

Gültepe-Turkey.name: Gültepe
other_names: Tepedesidelik an cemaat-i Mansurlu tabi-i Karacakürt
دپه دلك عن جماعت منصورلی تابع قره جه كورت

Asyut-Egypt.name: Asyut
Asyut-Egypt.evidence_basis: Upper Egypt administrative capital and Darb al-Arba'in caravan terminus; 1800 Description de l'Egypte, 1846 census, and 1882/1897/1907/1917 Egyptian Censuses.

Aden-Yemen.name: Aden
Aden-Yemen.evidence_basis: Medieval Indian Ocean port declining to ~1,500 by 1839 British seizure (Gavin 1975), booming as steamship coaling station in British Censuses of India (1872-1911).

Karbala-Iraq.name: Karbala
Karbala-Iraq.evidence_basis: Shi'i shrine city sacked by Wahhabis (1802) and Ottoman troops (1843), followed by Hindiyya canal and pilgrimage expansion (Nakash 1994; Cuinet 1894: 42,000).

Mansoura-Egypt.name: Mansoura
Mansoura-Egypt.evidence_basis: Daqahliyya capital and cotton-ginning center; 1800 Description de l'Egypte, 1846 census, and 1882/1897/1907/1917 Egyptian Censuses.

Gaziantep-Turkey.name: Gaziantep
Gaziantep-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1536 and 1574 Aintab tahrirs and court registers (Ozdeger 1988; Peirce 2003), textile/soap prosperity, Cuinet (1894: 43,150), and 1914 Aleppo Vilayet census.

Konya-Turkey.name: Konya
Konya-Turkey.evidence_basis: Capital of Karaman Eyalet; 1476, 1522, and 1584 Karaman tahrirs (Jennings 1976; Faroqhi 1984), Cuinet (1894: 44,000), and 1914 census.

Damanhur-Egypt.name: Damanhur
Damanhur-Egypt.evidence_basis: Beheira provincial capital on Cairo-Alexandria railway; 1800 Description de l'Egypte, 1846 census, and 1882/1897/1907/1917 Egyptian Censuses.

Hocalar-Turkey (3).name: Hocalar
other_names: خه وجه دیمكله مروف قره قوجه لر

Sivas-Turkey.name: Sivas
Sivas-Turkey.evidence_basis: Devastated by Timur's 1400 sack; 1455, 1520, and 1574 Rum Eyalet tahrirs (Faroqhi 1984; Demirel 1998), Cuinet (1894: 43,100), and 1914 census.

Trabzon-Turkey.name: Trabzon
Trabzon-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1486, 1523, and 1583 Trabzon tahrir defters (Lowry 1981), 19th-c. Persian transit trade boom, Cuinet (1894: 35,000), and 1914/1916-18 wartime records.

Tlemcen-Algeria.name: Tlemcen
Tlemcen-Algeria.evidence_basis: Zayyanid royal capital contracting under Ottoman provincialization (1555), recovering in French Recensements (1856, 1886: 28,204; 1911: 39,874).

Tripoli-Libya.name: Tripoli
Tripoli-Libya.evidence_basis: Ottoman conquest (1551), Karamanli dynasty (1711-1835), Ottoman Trablusgarp salnames, European consular reports, and 1911 Italian municipal enumeration (~45,000 walled/urban core).

Medina-Saudi Arabia.name: Medina
Medina-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Burckhardt (1815), Burton (1853), Hejaz salnames, 1908 Hejaz Railway terminus expansion (Ochsenwald 1984), and 1916-18 wartime civilian evacuation under Fakhri Pasha.

Sanaa-Yemen.name: Sanaa
Sanaa-Yemen.evidence_basis: Zaydi Imamate and Ottoman Yemen Vilayet capital (1547-1629, 1872-1918); Niebuhr (1763), Ottoman salnames, severe 1905 siege famine drop, and 1911 Treaty of Da'an stabilization.

Marash-Turkey.name: Marash
Marash-Turkey.evidence_basis: Dulkadirid capital annexed 1515; 1526 and 1563 Maras tahrirs (Yinanc & Elibuyuk 1988), Cuinet (1894: 40,000), and 1914 Aleppo Vilayet statistics.

Madinat al-Fayyum-Egypt.name: Madinat al-Fayyum
Madinat al-Fayyum-Egypt.evidence_basis: Fayum oasis agricultural capital; 1800 Description de l'Egypte, 1846 census, and 1882/1897/1907/1917 Egyptian Censuses.

Erzurum-Turkey.name: Erzurum
Erzurum-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1540/1591 Erzurum tahrirs after Safavid wars (Inalcik; Miroglu), 1829 Russo-Turkish war emigration, Cuinet (1894: 38,900), and 1915-18 WWI devastation (McCarthy 1983).

Annaba-Algeria.name: Annaba
Annaba-Algeria.evidence_basis: Ottoman coral and grain port (Bone) expanding rapidly as iron-ore and phosphate port under French rule (1856, 1886: 29,640; 1911: 42,039 Recensements).

Zagazig-Egypt.name: Zagazig
Zagazig-Egypt.evidence_basis: Founded c. 1830 by Muhammad Ali near Sharqiyya irrigation barrages; 1846 census and 1882/1897/1907/1917 Egyptian Censuses.

Jaffa-Palestine.name: Jaffa
Jaffa-Palestine.evidence_basis: Rebuilt late 18th c. and transformed by citrus exports, steamships, and 1892 Jerusalem railway (Ben-Arieh 1975; Kark 1990; 1914 Ottoman registers).

Gaza-Palestine.name: Gaza
Gaza-Palestine.evidence_basis: Largest town of 16th-c. Palestine in 1525/1556/1596 tahrirs (Cohen & Lewis 1978), 19th-c. barley/soap growth (Ben-Arieh 1975; Büssow 2011), and 1917 WWI evacuation.

Bitlis-Turkey.name: Bitlis
Bitlis-Turkey.evidence_basis: Sharafkhanid emirate and later vilayet capital; 1540 tahrir, Evliya Celebi, Cuinet (1894: 38,800), and severe 1915-18 WWI depopulation (McCarthy 1983).

Manisa-Turkey.name: Manisa
Manisa-Turkey.evidence_basis: Saruhanid and Ottoman princely seat; 1531 and 1575 Saruhan tahrir defters (Emecen 1989), 1831 census, and Cuinet (1894) / Aydin Vilayet salnames.

Diyarbakir-Turkey.name: Diyarbakir
Diyarbakir-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1518, 1540, and 1564 Amid tahrir defters (Goyunc 1969; Ilhan 2000), Cuinet (1894: 35,000), and 1914-18 Ottoman census / wartime losses.

Mahalla al-Kubra-Egypt.name: Mahalla al-Kubra
Mahalla al-Kubra-Egypt.evidence_basis: Principal Ottoman Delta textile center (Raymond 1984; 1800 Description de l'Egypte: ~17,500) and 1846/1882/1897/1907/1917 Egyptian Censuses.

Aydin-Turkey.name: Aydin
Aydin-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1530 and 1575 Aydin tahrirs (Faroqhi 1984), Meander cotton-railway growth (1866), and Cuinet (1894: 36,250) with 1914 salname.

Najaf-Iraq.name: Najaf
Najaf-Iraq.evidence_basis: Shi'i pilgrimage and hawza center; 18th-19th c. Persian endowment and canal growth (Nakash 1994), Cuinet (1894: 32,000), and Baghdad salnames.

Kuwait-Kuwait.name: Kuwait
Kuwait-Kuwait.evidence_basis: Founded c. 1716 by Bani Utub (Al Sabah); maritime pearling and dhow-building boom documented by Niebuhr (1765), Pelly (1863), and Lorimer Gazetteer (1908: 35,000).

Susuz-Turkey (2).name: Susuz
other_names: Susuz mahalle-i Demirli an cemaat-i Karacakürt
صوسز محلۀ تیمورلی عن جماعت قره جه كورت

Van-Turkey.name: Van
Van-Turkey.evidence_basis: Eastern frontier eyalet citadel; Ottoman salnames, Cuinet (1894: 30,000), 1914 census, and catastrophic 1915-18 WWI siege, deportations, and burning of the old city (McCarthy 1983).

Blida-Algeria.name: Blida
Blida-Algeria.evidence_basis: Andalusian refugee town founded c. 1535 in Mitidja plain; devastated by 1825 earthquake, rebuilt in French Recensements (1886: 24,304; 1911: 35,461).

Tripoli-Lebanon.name: Tripoli
Tripoli-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Mamluk provincial capital and Ottoman eyalet seat (1579); 1519/1571 Tripoli tahrirs (Raymond 1984), Cuinet (1896: 30,000), and 1914 Beirut Vilayet salname.

Minya-Egypt.name: Minya
Minya-Egypt.evidence_basis: Middle Egypt sugarcane and cotton rail hub; 1800 Description de l'Egypte, 1846 census, and 1882/1897/1907/1917 Egyptian Censuses.

Damietta-Egypt.name: Damietta
Damietta-Egypt.evidence_basis: Major Ottoman rice/linen port (~30,000 in 1800 Description de l'Egypte) that stagnated as Alexandria and Port Said rose (1846, 1882, 1897, 1907, and 1917 Egyptian Censuses).

Hodeidah-Yemen.name: Hodeidah
Hodeidah-Yemen.evidence_basis: Modest Tihama landing in Niebuhr (1763) rising to principal Ottoman Yemen Vilayet port after 1849/1872 reoccupation (Yemen salnames; Farah 2002).

Ankara-Turkey.name: Ankara
Ankara-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1522 (~3,000 hane) and 1571 Ankara tahrir defters during mohair (sof) boom (Ergenc 1995; Barkan), 17th-19th c. stagnation, Cuinet (1894: 28,000), and 1914 census.

Kirkuk-Iraq.name: Kirkuk
Kirkuk-Iraq.evidence_basis: Capital of Ottoman Shahrizor Eyalet; 16th-c. tahrir and military garrison records, Mosul Vilayet salnames, and Cuinet (1894: 28,000).

Tokat-Turkey.name: Tokat
Tokat-Turkey.evidence_basis: Silk caravan and copper-refining hub; 1574 tahrir (3,868 nefer) and 1643 mufassal avariz (3,858 nefer, Ozel 2004: +0.3% resilience), Cuinet (1894: 30,000).

Afyonkarahisar-Turkey.name: Afyonkarahisar
Afyonkarahisar-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1528 and 1572 Karahisar-i Sahip tahrirs (Faroqhi 1984), opium trade expansion, Cuinet (1894), and Hudavendigar Vilayet salnames.

Suez-Egypt.name: Suez
Suez-Egypt.evidence_basis: Ottoman Red Sea coffee and pilgrim port (Raymond 1984) expanded by 1858 railway and 1869 Suez Canal (1882/1897/1907/1917 Egyptian Censuses).

Hillah-Iraq.name: Hillah
Hillah-Iraq.evidence_basis: Euphrates agrarian market center; 16th-c. Baghdad tahrirs, 19th-c. traveler/consular reports and Hindiyya silting slowdown, Cuinet (1894: 28,000).

Jeddah-Saudi Arabia.name: Jeddah
Jeddah-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Ottoman Red Sea coffee and Hajj port; Burckhardt (1814: ~15,000), British/French consular reports, and post-1869 Suez Canal steamship growth (Ochsenwald 1984).

Harput-Turkey.name: Harput
Harput-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1566 tahrir (1,965 nefer) vs 1646 mufassal avariz (348 nefer, -82.3% Celali collapse, Ozel 2004); 19th-c. growth with Mezre/Mamuratulaziz (Cuinet 1894) and 1915-18 losses.

Eskisehir-Turkey.name: Eskisehir
Eskisehir-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1521 and 1572 Sultanoyugu tahrirs showing small market town prior to 1892 Anatolian Railway junction and Balkan/Crimean muhacir boom (Cuinet 1894; Karpat 1985).

Tekirdag-Turkey.name: Tekirdag
Tekirdag-Turkey.evidence_basis: Principal Thracian grain-export port provisioning Istanbul; 1530 Rumeli tahrir (Barkan), Edirne Vilayet salnames, and 1881-93/1914 censuses.

Antakya-Turkey.name: Antakya
Antakya-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1526/1570 Aleppo tahrirs, 1822 earthquake contraction, soap/silk trade recovery, Cuinet (1894: 23,500), and 1914 Aleppo Vilayet census.

Amasya-Turkey.name: Amasya
Amasya-Turkey.evidence_basis: Ottoman princely seat; 1576 tahrir (2,835 nefer) vs 1643 mufassal avariz (1,736 nefer, -38.8% Celali crisis drop, Ozel 2004), and Cuinet (1894: 25,000).

Mardin-Turkey.name: Mardin
Mardin-Turkey.evidence_basis: Artuqid citadel and Ottoman sanjak seat; 1518 and 1564 Mardin tahrirs (Goyunc 1969), Cuinet (1894: 25,000), and 1914 Diyarbakir salname.

Manama-Bahrain.name: Manama
Manama-Bahrain.evidence_basis: Gulf pearl-trade and entrepot capital; Portuguese/Safavid/Al Khalifa accounts and Lorimer Gazetteer (1908: ~25,000 town residents).

Hofuf-Saudi Arabia.name: Hofuf
Hofuf-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Capital of Ottoman Lahsa Eyalet (1550-1670) and Najd Sanjak (1871-1913); Palgrave (1862), Ottoman Basra salnames, and Lorimer Gazetteer (1908: ~25,000).

Izmit-Turkey.name: Izmit
Izmit-Turkey.evidence_basis: Marmara timber and naval shipyard port; 1530 Kocaeli tahrir, 1831 census, Cuinet (1894: 22,000), and 1914 independent sanjak statistics.

Erzincan-Turkey.name: Erzincan
Erzincan-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1516 and 1568 Erzincan tahrirs (Miroglu 1990), 1784 earthquake, Fourth Army HQ expansion (Cuinet 1894: 23,000), and 1915-18 frontline collapse.

Muscat-Oman.name: Muscat
Muscat-Oman.evidence_basis: Portuguese fortress (1507-1650) and Yaruba/Al Bu Sa'id maritime empire capital (incl. adjacent Matrah harbor); Lorimer Gazetteer (1908: ~24,000 combined urban complex).

Kutahya-Turkey.name: Kutahya
Kutahya-Turkey.evidence_basis: Germiyanid capital and seat of Anadolu Eyalet; 1530 and 1571 Kutahya tahrirs (Varlik 1974; Faroqhi 1984) and Cuinet (1894: 22,000).

Antalya-Turkey.name: Antalya
Antalya-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1530/1568 Teke tahrirs and archival 1831-1914 Ottoman census/salname series analyzed by Dayar (2023, Table 1), including Cuinet (1892: 24,631) and post-1897 stagnation.

Samsun-Turkey.name: Samsun
Samsun-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1576 tahrir (520 nefer) vs 1642 mufassal avariz (134 nefer, -74.2% crisis drop, Ozel 2004); post-1850 tobacco and steamship boom (Cuinet 1894: 16,000; 1914 census).

Nicosia-Cyprus.name: Nicosia
Nicosia-Cyprus.evidence_basis: 1570 Ottoman siege contraction, 1572 Ottoman Cyprus tahrir (Jennings 1993), 1831 Ottoman census, and exact British Cyprus Censuses (1881: 11,536; 1901: 14,752; 1911: 16,052).

Latakia-Syria.name: Latakia
Latakia-Syria.evidence_basis: 1519/1571 Tripoli tahrirs, 18th-19th c. tobacco export boom (Abu Riha), Cuinet (1896: 22,000), and Beirut Vilayet salnames.

Sousse-Tunisia.name: Sousse
Sousse-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Sahel olive-oil port expanded by modern harbor works (1899); Beylical tax registers and French Protectorate 1886/1911 censuses.

Malatya-Turkey.name: Malatya
Malatya-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1519 and 1560 Malatya tahrirs (Yinanc & Elibuyuk 1983), 1838 urban relocation to Aspuzu, Cuinet (1894: 20,000), and Mamuratulaziz salnames.

Kars-Turkey.name: Kars
Kars-Turkey.evidence_basis: Rebuilt by Murad III (1579) as eastern frontier fortress; Ottoman salnames until 1878 cession to Russia, then 1897 Russian Imperial Census (20,805) and 1914 Kavkazskiy Kalendar.

Nablus-Palestine.name: Nablus
Nablus-Palestine.evidence_basis: 1525, 1548, and 1596 Ottoman tahrirs (Cohen & Lewis 1978), olive-oil soap and cotton hinterland expansion (Doumani 1995), and 1914 Beirut Vilayet census.

Qena-Egypt.name: Qena
Qena-Egypt.evidence_basis: Upper Egyptian Nile-Quseir Red Sea caravan link and pottery town; 1800 Description de l'Egypte, 1846 census, and 1882-1917 Egyptian Censuses.

Tarsus-Turkey.name: Tarsus
Tarsus-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1519 and 1572 Tarsus tahrirs (Akis), Cilician cotton-ginning expansion, Cuinet (1894: 18,000), and Adana Vilayet salnames.

Bejaia-Algeria.name: Bejaia
Bejaia-Algeria.evidence_basis: Prosperous Hafsid port sharply contracted after 1510 Spanish conquest and 1555 Ottoman garrison era; French Recensements (1886: 10,491; 1911: 17,540).

Diriyah-Saudi Arabia.name: Diriyah
Diriyah-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Founded 1446; First Saudi State capital peaking at ~24,000 (Sadleir 1819; Vassiliev 1998) before total razing by Ibrahim Pasha of Egypt in 1818.

Zabid-Yemen.name: Zabid
Zabid-Yemen.evidence_basis: Rasulid and Tahirid scholarly capital contracting gradually during Ottoman and Qasimi centuries (Niebuhr 1763; Ottoman Yemen salnames).

Merzifon-Turkey.name: Merzifon
Merzifon-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1576 tahrir (1,783 nefer) vs 1643 mufassal avariz (957 nefer, -46.3% drop, Ozel 2004), 19th-c. textile/commercial revival, Cuinet (1894: 20,000).

Mostaganem-Algeria.name: Mostaganem
Mostaganem-Algeria.evidence_basis: Ottoman coastal garrison and Cheliff valley port; 18th-c. Algerian regency accounts and French Recensements (1856, 1886, 1911: 23,166).

Mus-Turkey.name: Mus
Mus-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1556 Mus tahrir, Bitlis Vilayet salnames, Cuinet (1894: 20,000), and 1915-17 WWI eastern front devastation (McCarthy 1983).

Isparta-Turkey.name: Isparta
Isparta-Turkey.evidence_basis: Hamid sanjak seat; 1522 and 1568 Hamid tahrirs (Faroqhi 1984), rose-oil and carpet export boom, Cuinet (1894: 20,000), and Konya salnames.

Kilis-Turkey.name: Kilis
Kilis-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1536 and 1570 Kilis tahrirs, olive-oil and soap hub north of Aleppo, Cuinet (1894: 20,000), and 1914 Aleppo Vilayet salname.

Haifa-Israel.name: Haifa
Haifa-Israel.evidence_basis: Relocated and walled by Zahir al-Umar (1761), booming after 1868 Templer colony and 1905 Hejaz Railway branch terminus (Yazbak 1998; Ben-Arieh 1975).

Sulaymaniyah-Iraq.name: Sulaymaniyah
Sulaymaniyah-Iraq.evidence_basis: Founded in 1784 by Ibrahim Pasha Baban as capital of the Baban Kurdish emirate; Rich (1820: ~10,000), Mosul Vilayet salnames, and Cuinet (1894: 18,000).

Rosetta-Egypt.name: Rosetta
Rosetta-Egypt.evidence_basis: Premier Ottoman Nile-mouth entrepot peaking in 18th c. (Raymond 1984), bypassed by 1820 Mahmudiyya Canal (1800 Description de l'Egypte; 1846-1917 Egyptian Censuses).

Kairouan-Tunisia.name: Kairouan
Kairouan-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Inland religious and wool/carpet center of Ottoman Tunisia; Beylical accounts (Valensi 1977) and French Protectorate 1886/1911 censuses.

Port Tawfîq-Egypt.name: Port Tawfîq
other_names: قسم أول ويتبعها بور توفيق والزيتيات والمنطقة السكنية التابعة لمعمل تكرير البترول الأميري الواقعة بالجزء الشرقي لشريط السكة الحديد

Balikesir-Turkey.name: Balikesir
Balikesir-Turkey.evidence_basis: Karesi sanjak capital; 1530 and 1573 tahrir defters, late 19th-c. muhacir resettlement, Cuinet (1894: 15,000), and 1914 Ottoman census.

Benghazi-Libya.name: Benghazi
Benghazi-Libya.evidence_basis: Rebuilt by Tripolitanian merchants and Ottoman garrison (1638); rapid late 19th-c. Wadai caravan and barley trade expansion in Ottoman salnames and 1911 Italian count.

Bizerte-Tunisia.name: Bizerte
Bizerte-Tunisia.evidence_basis: Andalusian-resettled corsair harbor transformed by 1895 French naval canal and base construction (1886 and 1911 Protectorate censuses).

Warrâq al-Hadar wa- Ambûba wa-Mît al-Nas.name: Warrâq al-Hadar wa- Ambûba wa-Mît al-Nasârâ

Mocha-Yemen.name: Mocha
Mocha-Yemen.evidence_basis: Global Red Sea coffee entrepot peaking in 17th-18th c. (Niebuhr 1763; Um 2009), collapsing in 19th c. due to harbor silting and competition from Aden and Hodeidah.

Denizli-Turkey.name: Denizli
Denizli-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1530 and 1571 tahrirs, 1678-1699 avariz registers showing 36.2% demographic contraction (Gokce 2000; Ozel 2004), and Cuinet (1894: 17,000).

Deir ez-Zor-Syria.name: Deir ez-Zor
Deir ez-Zor-Syria.evidence_basis: Small Euphrates town elevated to Ottoman independent mutasarrifate and garrison seat in 1864; Zor salnames, Cuinet (1894: 12,000), and 1914 census.

Hebron-Palestine.name: Hebron
Hebron-Palestine.evidence_basis: 1525, 1553, and 1596 tahrir defters (Cohen & Lewis 1978), glass/leather craft production, and 19th-early 20th c. counts (Ben-Arieh 1975; Jerusalem salnames).

Gelibolu-Turkey.name: Gelibolu
Gelibolu-Turkey.evidence_basis: First Ottoman European base (1354) and Kapudan Pasha naval arsenal; 1519/1530 Gelibolu tahrirs (Inalcik) and late Ottoman Edirne salnames.

Riyadh-Saudi Arabia.name: Riyadh
Riyadh-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Second Saudi capital (1824) after Diriyah's destruction; eyewitness counts by Palgrave (1862), Pelly (1865), Lorimer (1908), and Philby (1917).

Zahle-Lebanon.name: Zahle
Zahle-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Established early 18th c. as Bekaa Valley Greek Catholic commercial town; Mount Lebanon Mutasarrifate registers, Cuinet (1896: 14,500), and 1914 estimates.

Nevsehir-Turkey.name: Nevsehir
Nevsehir-Turkey.evidence_basis: Tiny village (Muskara) rebuilt into planned tax-exempt town by Grand Vizier Damat Ibrahim Pasha (1720-1730); 1831 census and Cuinet (1894: 15,800).

Kastamonu-Turkey.name: Kastamonu
Kastamonu-Turkey.evidence_basis: Candarid capital and Ottoman vilayet seat; 1530 and 1582 Kastamonu tahrirs, 1831 census, and Cuinet (1894: 15,600) with Kastamonu salnames.

Siirt-Turkey.name: Siirt
Siirt-Turkey.evidence_basis: Ottoman sanjak center under Diyarbakir/Bitlis Vilayets; 16th-c. tahrir estimates, Cuinet (1894: 15,000), and 1914 census.

Erbil-Iraq.name: Erbil
Erbil-Iraq.evidence_basis: Citadel town and lower bazaar on Mosul-Kirkuk highway; 1540/1575 tahrirs, 19th-c. traveler counts (Rich 1836), and Cuinet (1894: 14,000).

Hail-Saudi Arabia.name: Hail
Hail-Saudi Arabia.evidence_basis: Capital of the Rashidi Emirate of Jebel Shammar (1836-1921); eyewitness surveys by Wallin (1845), Palgrave (1862), Doughty (1877), Blunt (1879), and Lorimer (1908).

Yozgat-Turkey.name: Yozgat
Yozgat-Turkey.evidence_basis: Elevated from small village to regional capital c. 1740 by Capanoglu ayan dynasty; 1831 census, Cuinet (1894: 15,000), and 1914 Ankara salname.

Famagusta-Cyprus.name: Famagusta
Famagusta-Cyprus.evidence_basis: Rich Lusignan/Venetian entrepot reduced to fortress garrison after 1571 siege (Jennings 1993), reviving with Varosha harbor works (British Censuses 1881: 2,564; 1901: 3,134; 1911: 5,327).

Canakkale-Turkey.name: Canakkale
Canakkale-Turkey.evidence_basis: Founded around Mehmed II's 1462 Dardanelles fortress (Kale-i Sultaniye); Biga sanjak tahrirs, ceramics craft growth, Cuinet (1894: 11,500), and 1914 census.

Burdur-Turkey.name: Burdur
Burdur-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1522 and 1568 Hamid tahrirs, textile weaving town, 1831 census, and Cuinet (1894: 14,500) / Konya Vilayet salnames.

Usak-Turkey.name: Usak
Usak-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1520 and 1571 Kutahya tahrirs tracking famous Ottoman carpet-weaving guilds (Faroqhi 1984), 1831 census, and Cuinet (1894).

other_names: فجازلی عن جماعت قورتلی محلۀ قریق علی تابع بوینی اینجه لو

Tire-Turkey.name: Tire
Tire-Turkey.evidence_basis: Aydinid mint and leading 16th-c. textile town outranking Izmir in 1528/1575 Aydin tahrirs (Faroqhi 1984; Goffman 1990), stagnating later (Cuinet 1894: 14,000).

Corum-Turkey.name: Corum
Corum-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1520 and 1576 Corum tahrirs (Faroqhi 1984), 17th-c. Celali contraction, 1831 census, and Ankara Vilayet salnames / Cuinet (1894).

Salt-Jordan.name: Salt
Salt-Jordan.evidence_basis: 1538/1596 Ajlun tahrirs (Hutteroth & Abdulfattah 1977) and late Ottoman Balqa administrative/commercial expansion analyzed by Rogan (1999).

Giresun-Turkey.name: Giresun
Giresun-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1515 and 1583 Trabzon/Giresun tahrirs (Emecen 2005), 19th-c. hazelnut export expansion, Cuinet (1894: 10,500), and 1914 Trabzon salname.

Sidon-Lebanon.name: Sidon
Sidon-Lebanon.evidence_basis: Flourishing 17th-18th c. French silk/cotton trade seat under Fakhr al-Din II and Sayda Eyalet, eclipsed by Beirut in 19th c. (Philipp 2001; Cuinet 1896: 11,000).

Acre-Israel.name: Acre
Acre-Israel.evidence_basis: Ruined post-1291, revived as cotton-monopoly capital under Zahir al-Umar and Jazzar Pasha (1750-1804), then declined after 1840 bombardment and Haifa's rise (Philipp 2001).

Amara-Iraq.name: Amara
Amara-Iraq.evidence_basis: Founded in 1860 as an Ottoman Tigris garrison and Lynch river-steamer port; Basra Vilayet salnames, Cuinet (1894: 9,500), and British WWI intelligence handbooks.

Nasiriyah-Iraq.name: Nasiriyah
Nasiriyah-Iraq.evidence_basis: Founded in 1872 under Midhat Pasha and Shaykh Nasir al-Sadun as Muntafiq sanjak capital; Basra salnames and Cuinet (1894: 8,500).

Mugla-Turkey.name: Mugla

Nigde-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1522 and 1584 Karaman tahrir defters (Faroqhi 1984), 1831 census, and Konya Vilayet salnames / Cuinet (1894).

Nazareth-Palestine.name: Nazareth
Nazareth-Palestine.evidence_basis: 1596 tahrir village expanding into Galilee Christian pilgrimage and market town in 19th c. (Ben-Arieh 1975; Cuinet 1896; 1914 Ottoman census).

Bayburt-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1516 and 1568 Bayburt tahrirs (Miroglu 1975) along Trabzon-Erzurum caravan road, Cuinet (1894: 10,000), and 1916-18 WWI disruption.

Rize-Turkey.evidence_basis: 1523 and 1583 Trabzon tahrirs, linen (Rize bezi) export hub and Lazistan sanjak seat after 1878 Batumi cession (Cuinet 1894; Trabzon salnames).

Iskenderun-Turkey.evidence_basis: Aleppo's malarial coastal entrepot; English Levant Company consular accounts (17th-18th c.), 19th-c. marsh drainage and steamship growth (Cuinet 1894: 7,000).
